NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday stayed for a week the investigation against former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and others in the alleged CMRL bribery case.It also allowed them to approach a division bench of the Kerala High Court against a single judge's order directing the registration of an FIR.On October 9, the Kerala high court ordered the registration of an FIR under anti-corruption law against Vijayan and others, acting on a petition by advocate K M Shajahan.Also read - Kerala HC orders FIR against former CM Pinarayi Vijayan in CMRL bribery case The order followed a report submitted by the Enforcement Directorate (ED), which sought a probe into alleged payments made by Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) to Veena T, Vijayan's daughter, through her now-defunct company, Exalogic Solutions.The ED has alleged that CMRL made fraudulent payments of Rs 2.78 crore under the guise of IT consultancy services. It also allowed them to approach a division bench of the Kerala High Court against a single judge's order directing the registration of an FIR.

Article Title: Delhi high court cites national security, junks CIC order to IAF on PMs’ foreign trips
Article Text:
Delhi HC has set aside CIC order directing the IAF to disclose flight records PM Modi and former PM Manmohan Singh.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court has set aside a Central Information Commission order directing the Indian Air Force to disclose flight records pertaining to foreign visits undertaken by PM Narendra Modi and former PM Manmohan Singh, stating such disclosure could compromise national security and the PM’s safety.Allowing a petition by the Central Public Information Officer of Directorate of Personal Services, Air Headquarters, Justice Amit Mahajan held the IAF was justified in denying access to the records under section 8 of RTI that exempts disclosure of information that could jeopardise national security or pose a risk to a person’s life and physical safety.The high court said CIC erred in directing disclosure of Special Flight Returns (SFR-II) after redaction of the names and particulars of security personnel, observing removing such details would not necessarily eliminate the potential security risks.The RTI plea was filed by retired Commodore Lokesh K Batra in 2018, seeking information about foreign visits by Indian PMs on IAF aircraft from April 1, 2013, until the date of his application.In response, the IAF provided certain information about Modi’s foreign travels, and stated there had been no travel by ex-PM Singh on IAF aircraft during the period from April 1, 2013 to May 25, 2014. However, it refused to disclose copies of the SFR, Part-I and Part-II, citing national security concerns and the confidential nature of the records.Batra approached CIC, which directed the IAF on July 8, 2020, to provide certified copies of available and relevant SFR-II records to the applicant.The IAF challenged the CIC order, contending the records contained sensitive information that could potentially enable the identification of security personnel, reveal the composition of PM’s entourage and allow inferences to be drawn about patterns of security deployment.Justice Mahajan said, “The mere fact that public funds have been expended on the foreign visits of the PM does not, by itself, justify disclosure of information which may compromise the security arrangements put in place for such visits.”
Article Summary: Delhi HC has set aside CIC order directing the IAF to disclose flight records PM Modi and former PM Manmohan Singh. Delhi high court said CIC erred in directing disclosure of Special Flight Returns (SFR-II) after redaction of the names and particulars of security personnel.

Article Title: India & United States to boost defence, energy ties, Marco Rubio says trade deal close
Article Text:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and US ambassador to India Sergio Gor stand for the national anthem, as they attend a Freedom 250 reception at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

External affairs minister S Jaishankar met his US counterpart Marco Rubio in Mumbai, agreeing to further expand cooperation in energy, defence and technology ties and committing to an early conclusion of the trade deal still under discussion.While Rubio emphasised the role that the US can play in the diversification of India's energy and defence supplies, Jaishankar said in a post on X that they also discussed people-to-people ties, alluding to India's concerns over immigration and H-1B governance issues.Speaking at the US anniversary celebrations later, Jaishankar said in Rubio’s presence that Indian talent and skills have helped shape the tech era in the US.The ministers met ahead of a likely meeting between PM Narendra Modi and President Donald Trump next month in Manila on the margins of the ASEAN summit, and also before Modi's visit to the US in December for the G20. Both sides are also working to schedule a Quad leaders’ summit in Manila.A State Department readout said Jaishankar and Rubio discussed regional and global issues, including developments in West Asia. Rubio reiterated that increased energy trade with the US can play a transformative role in diversifying India’s supply chains while meeting its sizable consumer demand.Rubio’s second visit to India is taking place against the backdrop of US’ Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act meant to penalise countries purchasing Russian oil and Trump’s subsequent suspension temporarily of related tariffs. India maintains that its oil procurement is essential not just for its own energy security but also stability of the global markets. Rubio lauded “substantial progress” made by India in diversifying its energy portfolio.Rubio focused on reducing India's reliance on Russia also in defence as he stressed deepening of defence interoperability, framing enhanced technology purchases by India as a win-win situation for both nations.According to the US readout, Rubio also commended recent progress in bilateral defense and civil nuclear cooperation, and advocated increased purchase of US technologies and systems, which can enhance the security and prosperity of both countries.Rubio said in a post on X that he and Jaishankar reaffirmed the importance of advancing the US-India strategic partnership. The ministers will meet again on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta later this month. Both will also join their counterparts from Japan and Australia for a meeting of the Quad foreign ministers in Atlanta.According to the MEA, Jaishankar and Rubio welcomed the progress made in negotiations on the India–US Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) and reaffirmed their commitment to working towards its early conclusion. Rubio said both sides were “as close as you can be without having an executed agreement”.“I think there's a small number of items left to wrap up. So, I think that will happen shortly...and hopefully have some good news to announce fairly soon, and perhaps the leaders can sign it thereafter,” said Rubio, addressing the US travelling media.Shortly after his arrival, Rubio laid a wreath at Mumbai’s Taj Mahal Palace Hotel to honor the 26/11 terrorist attacks victims 166 victims, strongly condemning the attacks and reaffirming the US “unwavering solidarity” with the people of India.“Secretary Rubio underscored the Trump Administration’s commitment to dismantling terrorist networks and ensuring that those responsible for acts of terrorism are brought to justice, including individuals facing charges for their roles in planning the 2008 Mumbai attacks,” said the State Department, without naming Pakistan.According to the Indian readout, the visit reflected the sustained momentum of high-level exchanges between the two countries, underscoring the importance both sides attach to further advancing the India-US COMPACT for the 21st century. Modi and Trump had launched the COMPACT (Catalyzing Opportunities for Military Partnership, Accelerated Commerce & Technology) initiative last year to drive transformative change across key pillars of bilateral cooperation.
Article Summary: Jaishankar and Rubio agreed to further expand cooperation in energy, defence and technology ties. They also discussed people-to-people ties, alluding to India's concerns over immigration and H-1B governance issues. The ministers met ahead of a likely meeting between PM Narendra Modi and President Donald Trump next month.

Article Title: Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know
Article Text:
Reliance Industries Ltd, led by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, will continue to hold a majority stake in Jio Platforms following its stock market listing.

Jio Platforms IPO:

Jio IPO price band

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

India’s largest Initial Public Offering (IPO) till date opens for subscription on Wednesday. Jio Platforms plans to raise approximately Rs 30,213 crore through a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares.The public issue opens on October 21 and will remain available for subscription until October 23. This marks RIL Group's first IPO in nearly two decades.Reliance Industries Ltd, led by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, will continue to hold a majority stake in Jio Platforms following its stock market listing.From Jio IPO price band, listing date to GMP, we take a look at 10 important facts about the Jio IPO and what brokerages are saying:The company has fixed the price band at Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share. Based on the offer documents, the IPO values the company at around $108 billion. Investors will be able to apply for Jio Platforms shares in lots of 12, or in multiples of 12 shares.The company is also seeking to widen access to its IPO by setting aside portions of the issue for different investor groups.Eligible Reliance Industries shareholders have a reservation of up to Rs 2,500 crore, while eligible employees can apply under a reservation of up to Rs 500 crore.Retail individual investors will be eligible to subscribe to at least 35 per cent of the net offer.Jio Platforms will list on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE) on October 28, 2026.The Jio IPO is expected to surpass Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870 crore IPO in 2024, making it the largest public issue in India's history by value.The IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, meaning existing shareholders are not selling their holdings through the offering.Jio’s shares are trading at a grey market premium (GMP) of around 22%, signalling strong interest. On Tuesday, October 20, Jio Platforms shares were quoting at a grey market premium of about Rs 245.GMP refers to the premium that speculators in the unofficial market are prepared to pay for shares of a company awaiting its IPO listing.Based on the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 1,119, this indicates a possible listing price of Rs 1,364, implying a premium of nearly 22%, according to unofficial grey market quotes.Based on the current market capitalisation rankings on the BSE, the company would become India's fourth-most valuable listed company. It would rank behind RIL, valued at Rs 15.9 lakh crore, Bharti Airtel at Rs 11.2 lakh crore and HDFC Bank at nearly Rs 11 lakh crore.The BSE data also showed that Jio Platforms' valuation would be higher than those of ICICI Bank, State Bank of India and TCS. According to this TOI report , Reliance Industries (RIL) Group is poised to displace Tata Group as India's most valuable conglomerate once Jio Platforms makes its stock market debut, marking one of the biggest changes in the country's corporate pecking order in decades.At the upper end of its proposed price band of Rs 1,065-1,119 per share, Jio Platforms is expected to command a valuation of Rs 10.3 lakh crore. This would take the combined market capitalisation of the RIL Group to around Rs 28.5 lakh crore, putting it ahead of Tata Group's Rs 25.5 lakh crore as of October 15, according to ET Intelligence data.Before the proposed listing, RIL Group's market capitalisation stood at Rs 18.2 lakh crore.Adani Group currently occupies the third position among India's largest conglomerates, with a market capitalisation of Rs 17.48 lakh crore. It is followed by HDFC Group at Rs 13.91 lakh crore and Bajaj Group at Rs 13.88 lakh crore.Jio Platforms expects technology, artificial intelligence and cloud computing to fuel its next phase of expansion beyond telecom, Managing Director Akash Ambani told PTI."There is no either-or at Jio: the network is our technology," Ambani said in an interview with PTI. He pointed to the company's in-house 5G core, cloud-native radio access network and software platform, which serves 533.3 million customers.Satellite connectivity and next-generation 6G technology are among the other areas Jio has identified for future development.According to Ambani, the company's growth prospects are spread across several segments, from mobile services and home broadband to digital solutions for enterprises. He noted that around 26 crore Indians continue to use 2G services, while fixed broadband is available in only about 21 per cent of households across the country.In the decade since Reliance entered the telecom sector, Jio Platforms has built a subscriber base that places it among the world's largest mobile operators.Its operations now extend well beyond mobile connectivity, covering broadband, digital entertainment, cloud computing and enterprise services.Jio Platforms recorded revenue from operations of Rs 1.46 lakh crore in FY26, up from Rs 1.28 lakh crore in FY25. Net profit climbed to Rs 30,049 crore from Rs 26,109 crore over the same period, while EBITDA grew to Rs 76,255 crore from Rs 64,170 crore.Company figures reported for June 2026 show that Jio Platforms had 533.3 million subscribers and accounted for nearly 60% of India's data traffic.The IPO is also expected to improve Jio's financial position. The company plans to use up to Rs 27,500 crore of the net proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings owed by its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm.Jio's net debt-to-EBITDA ratio fell to 0.36 times in FY26, compared with 0.88 times in FY24, Akash Ambani said. He added that the IPO would give the company more financial headroom to invest in areas such as 5G, broadband, artificial intelligence, cloud computing and enterprise services.Jio's international technology investors, including Google and Meta, are also expected to contribute to its next stage of growth.Jio Platforms has allotted shares worth Rs 8,109.85 crore to 212 anchor investors at Rs 1,119 apiece, which is the upper end of its IPO’s price band.Institutional bids for the offering crossed a whopping Rs 2.5 lakh crore, which is more than 30 times the value of shares on offer in the anchor book.The company has allocated 7.24 crore shares.The scale of demand points to strong institutional interest in what is expected to be India's largest IPO.Life Insurance Corporation of India was the biggest recipient in the anchor allotment, securing shares worth Rs 499.98 crore. New World Fund Inc received shares of Rs 486.27 crore, while the Government of Singapore was allotted Rs 340.93 crore.SBI Focused Fund secured an allocation worth Rs 315 crore, followed by BNP Paribas Financial Markets - ODI, which received shares valued at Rs 303.25 crore.Domestic mutual funds were allotted 2.489 crore shares worth Rs 2,784.96 crore, which is 34.34% of the anchor book.Several major international investment firms also participated in the anchor book. These included BlackRock, Capital Group, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, Schroders, JPMorgan Asset Management, Franklin Templeton and Janus Henderson.Brokerages have expressed optimism about the offering, pointing to Jio's leading position in the telecom sector, improving profitability and potential for expansion in broadband and artificial intelligence.Motilal Oswal Wealth Management has advised investors to subscribe to the Jio IPO, citing potential listing gains as well as long-term investment prospects. The brokerage pointed to the company's strong position in India's telecom market and its improving earnings performance. It said Jio's extensive subscriber base, in-house technology capabilities and growing broadband business offer a solid platform for further expansion.The brokerage noted that Jio had 533 million subscribers as of June 2026 and accounted for around 60% of India's wireless data traffic. It also sees scope for growth in digital services, backed by Jio's proprietary 5G technology, more than 7,200 patent applications and investments in cloud computing and artificial intelligence.Canara Bank Securities has also recommended subscribing to the issue with a long-term investment horizon. According to the brokerage, Jio stands to gain as customers shift from 2G to 4G and 5G services, home broadband adoption expands and the company explores opportunities to monetise its technology in international markets.Canara Bank Securities identified Jio's in-house technology portfolio, spanning its 5G network, broadband solutions and JioBrain AI platform, as potential drivers of future revenue growth.
Article Summary: India’s largest Initial Public Offering (IPO) till date opens for subscription on Wednesday. Jio Platforms plans to raise approximately Rs 30,213 crore through a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares. Reliance Industries Ltd, led by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, will continue to hold a majority stake in Jio.

Article Title: India-New Zealand FTA kicks in: Zero duty, more opportunities - what's in it for India?
Article Text:
India - New Zealand trade deal kicks in

What's in it for India?

1. Duty-free access for Indian exporters

2. A boost for MSMEs and small businesses

3. New opportunities for farmers

4. More opportunities for Indian professionals and students

5. Investment, manufacturing and employment

6. Safeguards for sensitive Indian sectors

7. A larger trade partnership

NEW DELHI: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) came into force on Tuesday opening up new opportunities for Indian exporters, manufacturers, farmers, professionals and businesses. The agreement provides 100% duty-free access to the New Zealand market for all Indian export tariff lines, removing peak tariffs of up to 10%.Signed on April 27, 2026, the pact aims to deepen economic ties between the two countries and double bilateral trade in goods and services to NZ$7 billion (Rs 35,000 crore) by 2030. Negotiations were launched on March 16, 2025, and concluded on December 22, 2025, within nine months.The agreement is India's 17th operational FTA and the seventh trade pact to come into force in the past five years. It covers goods, services, investment, agriculture, skills and mobility, while retaining safeguards for sensitive sectors.All Indian goods can enter New Zealand duty-free, giving Indian exporters a competitive advantage and placing them on a level playing field with New Zealand's other FTA partners.Textiles, apparel, leather, footwear, gems and jewellery, engineering goods, automobiles and auto components, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, agricultural products and processed foods are among the sectors expected to benefit.Duty-free access for wooden logs, coking coal and metal waste and scrap will strengthen manufacturing and MSME supply chains. Streamlined regulatory processes are expected to benefit pharmaceutical and medical device industries.The agreement opens New Zealand's market to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), women-led businesses, start-ups, artisans and first-generation entrepreneurs.Zero duties and faster customs processes are expected to reduce landed costs and help Indian businesses expand their customer base. Cooperation will improve access to trade-related information and links with New Zealand's small and medium enterprise ecosystem, with particular attention to businesses owned by women and young people.New Zealand has also committed to facilitating the registration of Indian geographical indications (GIs), creating opportunities to protect products associated with rural artisans and traditional industries.The Agricultural Productivity Partnership will bring technology, training and global best practices to Indian agriculture, extending cooperation beyond tariff concessions.Dedicated action plans for apples, kiwifruit and honey will support better orchard management, reduce post-harvest losses and improve productivity and farm incomes. Cooperation will also cover horticulture, forestry, livestock and fisheries.New Zealand will provide technical assistance to establish Centres of Excellence for kiwifruit, apples and honey. Phase I sites for kiwifruit centres have been identified at Pfutsero in Nagaland and Magra in Uttarakhand. Two apple centres are proposed in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, while honey centres are envisaged in Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.Tariff rate quotas for apples, kiwifruit and Mānuka honey are linked to the delivery of action plans and overseen by a Joint Agriculture Productivity Council, linking market access with farmer welfare.New Zealand has offered market access in around 118 services sectors and Most-Favoured-Nation commitments in about 139 sub-sectors, its most extensive services offered under any trade agreement to date.For the first time, dedicated access has been provided for health and traditional medicine services, including Ayurveda, yoga and other AYUSH systems.Indian youth and professionals will have access to 5,000 Temporary Employment Entry visas and 1,000 Working Holiday visas annually.There will be no numerical cap on Indian students. Post-study work rights will extend to three years for STEM bachelor's and master's graduates and up to four years for doctoral scholars.New Zealand has committed to facilitating $20 billion in investment into India over more than 15 years.The investment is expected to benefit agriculture, manufacturing, infrastructure and start-ups, supporting innovation, entrepreneurship and employment generation under the Make in India vision.Provisions covering duty-free inputs, bilateral cumulation, customs facilitation and investment promotion could encourage deeper integration into value chains and improve investment conditions.Dairy, sugar, edible oils and key agricultural commodities remain excluded from concessions to protect farmers, dairy producers, fisherfolk and rural communities.Rules of Origin, a bilateral safeguard mechanism and anti-circumvention provisions aim to ensure that benefits reach genuine Indian exporters.Bilateral trade fell about 11% to $1.15 billion in 2025-26, from $1.3 billion in the previous fiscal year. India's exports stood at $566.51 million, while imports were $589.1 million, leaving a trade deficit of $22.59 million.The FTA seeks to reverse the limited scale of trade and expand economic engagement. The first-ever export of a JCB machine from India to New Zealand was flagged off at the entry-into-force ceremony, with further product flag-offs planned across agriculture, gems and jewellery, engineering, sporting goods, footwear and leather.Commerce minister Piyush Goyal said that the agreement would create opportunities for exporters, particularly MSMEs, artisans, farmers and women entrepreneurs. The pact also supports India's strategic partnership with New Zealand and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, with its success ultimately depending on businesses converting improved market access into actual trade and investment.
Article Summary: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) came into force on Tuesday. The agreement provides 100% duty-free access to the New Zealand market for all Indian export tariff lines, removing peak tariffs of up to 10%. The pact aims to deepen economic ties between the two countries.

Article Title: In talks with Reliance to refine more Venezuelan oil: US secretary of state Marco Rubio
Article Text:
Marco Rubio at the 26/11 memorial at Taj Mahal Palace Hotel in Mumbai.

MUMBAI/ DELHI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio Tuesday said US was in discussions with Reliance Industries on creating capacity to refine Venezuelan crude, calling India a refining superpower and underlining that Washington understood India’s need to diversify its oil imports and saw Venezuela as a potential source of supply.Rubio is visiting Jamnagar Wednesday to tour the Reliance refinery and, in a lastminute change of schedule, is likely to spend the night there. He was earlier scheduled to leave around 9pm and return to Mumbai. In Jamnagar, he will have dinner with Mukesh Ambani at the Vantara centre.Rubio’s visit to Jamnagar comes within weeks of a vicious attack on Ambani by Elon Musk, who even addressed him as “PM Ambani”.Before his departure for Jamnagar, Rubio will meet Gautam Adani and Tata group chief N Chandrasekaran in Mumbai.Rubio, speaking to the media in Mumbai, said Reliance had previously operated in Venezuela and had the refining capabilities to process heavy crude oil. As Venezuelan oil production increases, the Indian company could play a role in processing more of the country’s output, he said, adding that the discussions would continue.“India is a refining superpower,” Rubio said, noting that Reliance had existing oil concessions in Venezuela and had refined its crude in the past.“We’ll see how the conversation goes,” he said.On India’s purchase of Russian oil, Rubio said New Delhi had repeatedly expressed its desire to diversify its energy portfolio, describing it as a sensible strategy. He acknowledged shifting supply sources could not be achieved overnight but said India had made substantial progress.“In the end, it’s not just about Russian oil; it’s about their desire to diversify,” he said, adding US was keen to be a source of energy supplies for India.Washington had discussed Venezuela and other countries as potential sources, he said, arguing a diverse energy portfolio was in the interests of both.
Article Summary: Rubio is visiting Jamnagar Wednesday to tour the Reliance refinery. In a lastminute change of schedule, he is likely to spend the night there. He will have dinner with Mukesh Ambani at the Vantara centre.

Article Title: India, US ‘perfectly aligned’ on key issues: Marco Rubio; defends ties with Pakistan
Article Text:
Rubio is set to visit Jamnagar for talks on bilateral ties, energy cooperation and commercial investment.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US secy of state defends ties with Pakistan

US secretary of state Marco Rubio urged businesses to view the India-US relationship as a strategic partnership spanning technology, trade and security, saying the two countries were “perfectly aligned” on issues that would shape the 21st century, even as he acknowledged that disagreements between them would persist.Addressing a gathering of India Inc’s leading business figures at a Freedom 250 event at BKC, Rubio said the relationship between the two countries could help shape the future of the global economy, particularly as advances in artificial intelligence and quantum computing transform industries and societies.“I truly believe the relationship between US and India is defining, in many ways, in a positive way, what the 21st century can look like,” he said.The gathering included Noel Tata (Tata Trusts), Anand Mahindra (Mahindra Group), Kiran MazumdarShaw (Biocon), Ashok P Hinduja (Hinduja Group), Amit Dixit (Blackstone), Hitendra Dave (HSBC India), K Balasubramanian (Citi India) and Rahul Badhwar (JPMorgan Chase).Rubio identified emerging technologies and secure trade routes as two areas in which the countries’ interests converge. “US and India are perfectly aligned,” he said, referring to the challenge of harnessing new technologies for public benefit.“We have the same expertise. We have the same talented people working on it, from engineers to creative thinkers and innovators.”He linked economic growth to the security of international shipping routes, arguing that businesses needed the freedom to move goods across borders and reach markets.For India and US, he said, this required “a free and secure Indo-Pacific” in which “no nation can claim dominance or ownership of international shipping lanes”.“No two nations on earth will ever be perfectly aligned on every issue,” he said. “But on the core issues that matter..., alignment between our countries is extraordinary.”The speech did not signal any immediate change in tariffs or market access.Rubio said he believed US should engage more frequently with India, and he planned to return in three months.US is required to have relationships with countries, including with those with whom it may have some disagreements, said secretary of state Marco Rubio while defending ties with Pakistan and condemning terrorism. Rubio also confirmed the next Quad leaders’ summit would take place in Manila next month.“In the case of Pakistan, it’s a country that we have to have a relationship with, a country that possesses nuclear weapons. It’s a country that from a geographic standpoint, we need to be able to interact with them in much the same way as govt of India has to have and has a relationship and meets with leaders from Iran,” said Rubio speaking to Network 18.“... It could be a positive thing because if... we can speak to them, it perhaps puts us in a position to help discourage the kinds of things India is worried about,” he added.
Article Summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio urged businesses to view the India-US relationship as a strategic partnership spanning technology, trade and security. Rubio said the two countries were “perfectly aligned” on issues that would shape the 21st century, even as he acknowledged that disagreements between them would persist.

Article Title: US allows mining firm Sherritt to deliver fuel to Cuba
Article Text:
US allows mining firm Sherritt to deliver fuel to Cuba. (File photo)

(From news agency AFP)

HAVANA: Mining company Sherritt, which halted operations in Cuba over US sanctions, on Tuesday said Washington was allowing it to send fuel and other materials needed for nickel extraction to the island.The Canadian firm has mined nickel and cobalt in a joint venture with Cuba's state-owned General Nickel Company S.A. since the 1990s.Tuesday's announcement aims to allow a future resumption of its activities at the Moa mine after US sanctions pushed it to withdraw from the country in early May.Soon afer its withdrawal, however, Sherritt reversed the decision to liquidate its assets and said it was negotiating the sale of 55 percent of its shares with Gillon Capital -- a deal that would make the US firm Sherritt's majority shareholder.Gillon is owned by Ray Washburne, who served as president of the US government's development finance institution during President Donald Trump's first stint in the White House."The Fuel License" granted by the US Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) "authorizes the sale, transportation, export, delivery and payment for fuel, fuel oil, and sulfur to Moa Nickel, together with all related services," Sherritt stated.Talks with OFAC, the body that doles out Cuba sanctions, took place in close coordination with Gillon Capital, according to Tuesday's statement."The actual restart of operations at Moa Nickel remains subject to receipt of a second OFAC emergency license," it added.Washington imposed an energy blockade on Cuba in January, allowing only fuel shipments from the US and destined for the private sector to get through.Trump has openly mused about seizing control of the island, claiming that it poses a threat to US national security.
Article Summary: US allows mining firm Sherritt to deliver fuel to Cuba. Canadian firm has mined nickel and cobalt in joint venture with Cuba's state-owned General Nickel Company S.A. since the 1990s. Washington imposed an energy blockade on Cuba in January, allowing only fuel shipments from the US.

Article Title: BJP’s delimitation gambit: Will it isolate Congress, puncture opposition’s SIR unity?
Article Text:
Parliament’s Monsoon Session has remained prorogued for 68 days after being adjourned sine die and the opposition has questioned this delay.

A look at how the number of seats may change based on estimates.

Kharge's missives to PM Modi

Rijiju's sharp response to Kharge

Amit Shah dismissed concerns that delimitation would disadvantage southern states.

Why are opposition parties worried

The SIR unity vs Delimitation dilemma

Keen political contest

NEW DELHI: Is the government planning a new delimitation push to puncture the Congress ’s bid to unite the opposition with protests against SIR? Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju has refuelled buzz that Parliament may be called for a short session to take up the legislation while also signalling Congress’s isolation on the issue by rejecting its demands for all-party consultations.The government had tried to push through a Constitution Amendment Bill in April this year in Lok Sabha but failed. The proposed legislation, which aimed at implementing 33% reservation for women in legislatures from 2029 and increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats to 850 did not get the mandatory two-thirds majority. The bill received 298 votes in favour and 230 against. It needed support of at least 352 out of the 528 members who were present and voted.The Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13, 2026. It has been 68 days since then. However, the session is yet to be prorogued. This gap has broken the previous record of a 28-day delay for the Monsoon Session in 2015 and has left the opposition, especially the Congress, worried.The Congress fears the government has been engaging in backroom moves with other parties in the opposition camp to cobble up a two-thirds majority and get the two Bills passed.An anxious Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has written four letters to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the last one four days ago. The Congress has been trying to pre-empt a sudden, surprise push by the government to pass the delimitation and women’s reservation bills."You may kindly recall that I had first written to you on April 11, 2026, to convene an All-Party meeting before bringing any Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation. You did not do so. Thereafter, you made the Bills public on the late evening of April 14, 2026 and convened a special session on April 16, 2026. The Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation failed to muster the necessary two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha on April 17, 2026, by a decisive margin," said Kharge in his letter."Thereafter, on July 16, 2026 and August 27, 2026, I wrote to you again, repeating our request for an All-Party meeting. I am now doing so for a fourth time," the Congress chief said.Kharge cautioned the government against taking a unilateral approach on major constitutional reforms such as national delimitation, which directly affects parliamentary constituency boundaries and regional representation.In a sharp response to Kharge's Oct 16 letter to the Prime Minister, Rijiju said, "When after repeated requests Congress didn't give dates for discussion, govt's outreach extended to other political parties. Consultations were held with representatives of parties including SP, DMK, YSRCP, NCP (SP), Shiv Sena (UBT), AIMIM and BJD with a view to building a broader consensus in support of the proposed legislation. "Rijiju also rejected Kharge’s concerns over the “unprecedented” delay in proroguing the Monsoon session. Dismissing Kharge’s contention, Rijiju cited precedents and underlined that no constitutional requirement existed prescribing a specific period within which a House must be prorogued following its adjournment sine die."The mere fact that a House has not been prorogued does not, by itself, give rise to any constitutional or procedural impropriety or irregularity," Rijiju said.When Parliament is adjourned sine die and not prorogued, it can be convened for a session at short notice. Sine die adjournment means that the session is suspended indefinitely without setting a day for reconvening. It does not mean a formal end of the session, which requires an official prorogation order by the President of India. There is no specific timeframe for prorogation of Parliament after a session has been adjourned sine die. But normally this happens within a few days.Since the Delimitation Bill is a Constitution Amendment Bill and cannot be taken through an ordinance route it makes sense for the government to keep the option alive by not proroguing the session.For the opposition, this is a clear signal that the government is still trying to get the numbers. And that brings us to the second question of opposition unity.The last few weeks have seen the opposition at its united best. The protests against SIR has seen the Congress not just reach out to but also accommodate every opposition party. There have been differences and some reports of one-upmanship, but by and large all parties have been together under the INDIA bloc. The DMK and AAP despite staying away from the opposition coalition’s prorgrammes are united in the cause. In fact, the DMK has sent mixed signals - supporting the agitation against NEET but also accusing the Congress of duplicity citing its support to VIjay and the TVK government in Tamil Nadu. The AAP, on the other hand, has been active with the Cockroach Janata Party and has actively joined their protest programmes. Then there are parties which have been on both sides, like the Shiv Sena (UBT), Mamata Banerjee.In fact, Naveen Patnaik’s Biju Janata Dal of Odisha that normally keeps equal distance from both the NDA and the INDIA bloc also joined one of the protests in Delhi to show solidarity with the cause.And it's not just political parties; several civil society groups have also joined the INDIA bloc platform, amplifying the demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the reversal of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which has led to huge deletions of voters in several poll-bound states.Interestingly, many political parties named by Kiren Rijiju in his statement have been part of the ongoing protests against SIR under the INDIA bloc. Some that haven’t joined the common protest have expressed solidarity with the cause and have protested separately.This clearly poses a challenge to opposition unity. The Congress and many other opposition parties have been against the SIR and also the Delimitation Bill. However, while many of them are with the Congress on the issue of SIR, their independent negotiations with the government on the Delimitation Bill will keep the grand-old-party worried.The BJP has reached out to several regional parties with an assurance that the proposed delimitation bill will not change the representation of states in Parliament, as the seats in Lok Sabha will be increased 50% across the states and not in proportion to the existing population as it should normally be under the delimitation process.The BJP-led NDA government’s move to tag the women’s reservation bill, which proposes to increase their representation in Lok Sabha, comes as an added pressure as well as incentive. If the parties oppose, they are labelled as anti-women by the BJP and its ruling allies in their respective states. On the other hand, if they accept the proposal, they get the benefit of accommodating additional women without impacting the existing dominance of men.Clearly, this is going to be a keen contest between the BJP and the Congress. It will be interesting to see how the Congress manages to persuade its allies to stay united against BJP’s Delimitation plans. If some regional parties like the DMK, which are very unhappy with the Congress do decide to back the delimitation bill, will it take the sting out of the present SIR campaign?The Congress, anyways, needs to realise that SIR cannot be the only glue that will hold together the opposition parties. The Supreme Court is already hearing a clutch of SIR related petitions. Also, the Election Commission has started the process re-enrolment of voters and also of SSR, the Special Summary revision of electoral rolls, in 14 states and 3 Union Territories. So, SIR as a unifying bond may not help the Congress for long. The main opposition party needs to find lasting ways of ensuring that all its allies are united against the government.
Article Summary: Parliament’s Monsoon Session has remained prorogued for 68 days after being adjourned sine die and the opposition has questioned this delay. Congress fears the government has been engaging in backroom moves with other parties in the opposition camp to cobble up a two-thirds majority and get the two Bills passed.

Article Title: 'Expect partners to show zero tolerance on terrorism': EAM thanks US for handing over Tahawwur Rana

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Tuesday hailed ties between India and the US, saying the partnership between the two countries had grown over the past few decades despite their share of differences.Addressing the Freedom 250 reception in Mumbai, Jaishankar said Indian talent and skills had helped shape the technology era in the US.“Our ties have indeed come a long way. History records that many Americans were supportive of India's struggle for independence. After that, whether it was infrastructure and education or food, agriculture, and technology, our partnership has made a real difference to India's development. Indian talent and Indian skills have helped shape the tech era in the United States. Of course, we've had our share of issues, including the manner in which we approach the world and its challenges,” he said.“But in the last few decades, our partnership has steadily expanded, acquiring new dimensions and new facets. The Quad, Mission 500, Pax Silica, and the Forge Initiative are among some of the notable examples. Growth in the fields of energy, defence, and civil aviation has actually been striking,” he added.Jaishankar also thanked Washington for its decision to extradite Tahawwur Hussain Rana, a key conspirator in the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, to India. He said New Delhi expected its partners to show zero tolerance towards terrorism.“Secretary Rubio, all of Mumbai, and indeed all of India, appreciate your laying a wreath today at the Taj Hotel's 26/11 Memorial. India also welcomes this administration's decision to extradite Tahawwur Hussain Rana, who was one of the key culprits. We are clear on our right to defend ourselves against terrorism and expect our partners to show zero tolerance toward terrorism as well,” Jaishankar said.“As we mark this anniversary together, it is natural to reflect on the way ahead. The world order is clearly in transition, and countries are responding accordingly. Each one of us will naturally pursue our national interests. In such an era, expanding our convergence is key to deepening our ties. There are new opportunities in our partnership in trade, investment, technology, and energy, and these await us. We have a shared stake in strengthening peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific. Engaging regularly and identifying common interests will certainly help provide a pathway,” he added.The remarks came as US secretary of state Mark Rubio began a three-day visit to India. Earlier in the day, Jaishankar hosted his US counterpart for wide-ranging talks shortly after Rubio arrived in Mumbai for his second visit to India in less than five months.Following the meeting, Jaishankar said in a social media post that the two had “shared views on further advancement of our ties, focusing on trade, energy, technology, defence and people-to-people ties”.The US state department said the two leaders discussed regional and global issues, including developments in West Asia.“The secretary reiterated that increased energy trade with the United States can play a transformative role in diversifying India's supply chains while meeting its sizable consumer demand,” it said.“He also commended recent progress in bilateral defence and civil nuclear cooperation, and advocated for the increased purchase of US technologies and systems, which can enhance the security and prosperity of both our countries,” the state department added.
Article Summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar hailed ties between India and the US. He said the partnership between the two countries had grown over the past few decades. The remarks came as US secretary of state Mark Rubio began a three-day visit to India.

Article Title: No double standards on terror, need unified action to dismantle its entire ecosystem: Rajnath at SCO
Article Text:

Defence minister Rajnath Singh , in the presence of Pakistan’s deputy PM and foreign minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar at a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting in Dushanbe, said on Tuesday that there should not be “double standards” on terrorism as it “not only harms innocent lives but also investment and commerce”.Addressing the 25th meeting of the council of heads of govt (CHG) of SCO, Rajnath called upon member states to make concerted efforts to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism, describing the menace as one of the gravest threats to peace and development. “Terrorism results in the loss of innocent lives and disrupts investment and commerce. It radicalises societies and deprives youth of the opportunities they rightfully deserve. There can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards in addressing it, and no place for those who finance, support, or provide safe havens to terrorists,” he said.Hinting at the supply chain disruptions due to the West Asia conflict, Rajnath, who represents India on behalf of PM Narendra Modi, said, “In the changing global economic environment, SCO countries will have to work together on resilient supply chains, better trade and investment, and technology-driven development.India's vision is clear—ensuring inclusive development for all member countries through security, connectivity, and opportunity. ”Pointing out that India supports initiatives that link markets, facilitate trade and create new avenues for development, the minister said that initiatives such as the International North-South Transport Corridor and the Chabahar Port can contribute significantly to connecting Central Asia with broader markets. Stressing that the benefits of economic cooperation must reach all sections of society, he reaffirmed India’s support for the adoption of an action plan for the multilateral trade and economic cooperation programme for the period 2026-2030.The minister stressed that connectivity must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries, adding that projects not founded on these principles will not be sustainable. He emphasised the need to move beyond physical connectivity by simplifying customs procedures, promoting digital documentation, improving logistics and adopting interoperable digital solutions to reduce the cost of doing business across the region. He urged the SCO to build on the strong foundation established over the past 25 years and chart a forward-looking roadmap focused on consensus-driven cooperation and tangible outcomes.Rajnath recalled the deliberations at the SCO Summit in Bishkek in Aug-Sept, when PM Modi underlined the need for concrete steps by the organisation on issues related to security, connectivity, and opportunity. “India believes that the SCO must remain efficient and steadfast in its adherence to the principles of sovereign equality, consensus, and mutual respect. A greater number of institutions does not necessarily translate into greater achievements. New mechanisms should focus on clearly identified needs, avoid duplication, and prioritise delivering practical value to Member States,” he said.Later at a meeting with the Indian diaspora in Dushanbe, the minister said, “Guided by the philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, India aspires to become a nation that combines prosperity, knowledge and strength with a commitment to global peace and the well-being of humanity”. Highlighting India’s growth trajectory, Rajnath stated that the country contributes more than 16% to global economic growth and is growing at approximately 7.8%, even as several major economies face a slowdown.He emphasised that India’s economic transformation, reform-driven governance, technological advancement and growing global stature under PM Modi’s leadership are paving the way towards the realisation of this vision.Highlighting India’s growth trajectory, Rajnath stated that the country contributes more than 16% to global economic growth and is growing at approximately 7.8%, even as several major economies face a slowdown. Referring to the changing global trade landscape, he said that India has entered into free trade agreements with 38 countries, opening new markets for Indian manufacturers and producers.He stated that the India-UK and India-EU trade agreements, which are expected to eliminate tariffs on 99% of Indian exports to these markets, would strengthen the country’s trade prospects and global economic partnerships.
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh called upon member states to make concerted efforts to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism. “Terrorism results in the loss of innocent lives and disrupts investment and commerce. It radicalises societies and deprives youth of the opportunities they rightfully deserve,” he said.

NEW DELHI: An Air India Express flight from Bhogapuram in Andhra Pradesh to Bengaluru suffered a bird strike but landed safely at Kempegowda International Airport, with all 148 passengers and crew members unharmed on Tuesday.The incident occurred on Monday, following which the aircraft was inspected by technical teams to assess any damage to its structure and engines. Such inspections are part of standard safety procedures after a bird strike to determine whether an aircraft can continue operating safely.An Air India Express spokesperson said the aircraft had been declared serviceable after the inspection and that there was no disruption to flight operations."Our Bhogapuram-Bengaluru flight reported a bird strike. The aircraft was inspected and has been declared serviceable. There has been no impact on our operations," the spokesperson said in a statement, as quoted by ANI.A similar incident was reported on October 17, when an Emirates flight from Dubai to Delhi suffered a bird strike while arriving in the national capital. The incident damaged the aircraft's nose cone and delayed its return flight to Dubai by more than 14 hours as repairs were required, according to reports.Bird strikes occur when birds collide with aircraft, potentially damaging components such as the nose, windscreen or engines. While many such incidents cause little or no damage, they can require technical inspections and repairs before an aircraft is cleared for its next flight.
Article Summary: Air India Express flight from Bhogapuram in Andhra Pradesh to Bengaluru suffered a bird strike. The aircraft was inspected by technical teams to assess any damage to its structure and engines. Such inspections are part of standard safety procedures to determine whether an aircraft can continue operating safely.

Article Title: Bhagwat warns protests can become political tools, urges restraint from govt too
Article Text:
“India is ultimate target”: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on ‘regime change’ efforts, calls for restraint in protests

NEW DELHI: Warning that when a movement becomes “a tool of politics”, forces seeking to undermine India take advantage, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Tuesday linked political protests and distrust of institutions to alleged foreign attempts to destabilise the country. But his Vijayadashami address in Nagpur also carried a message for governments: respect citizens' dignity, act within constitutional limits and avoid deepening divisions while addressing grievances.The remarks came amid protests over the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. Bhagwat did not name the Commission, SIR or any political party, nor did he present evidence connecting the protests with foreign forces.The warning was not new. In 2023, Bhagwat had identified “cultural Marxists” and “Woke” forces as promoting anarchy through education, media and public discourse. In 2024, he invoked the “Deep State”, alleging attempts to foster grievances and distrust of institutions. His 2025 Vijayadashami address warned against forces seeking to reproduce political upheavals witnessed in neighbouring countries.What's different this year was the emphasis: instead of naming ideological adversaries, Bhagwat described their alleged methods, from deepening disagreements and cultivating a sense of victimhood to undermining faith in national institutions and drawing domestic political actors into the process.Claiming that powers seeking to install proxies in other countries regarded India's rise as a threat, he said: “They devise plans and work towards finding ways to dismantle Bharat, Hindu society, and Sangh.” Some ambitious political leaders, driven by “petty political interests”, joined such efforts, he alleged, without identifying them.Yet Bhagwat acknowledged the legitimacy of grievances. “In our vast society problems do exist. There are likely to be numerous shortcomings in the system as well. It is only natural that these may lead to agitations,” he said. “However, such agitations should aim to provide solutions.”He applied that standard to protesters, political leaders and the state alike, asking them not to create “discord, animosity, resentment, bitterness, or divisions”. Even when emotions ran high, their actions should remain within the Constitution and law. He warned that “the lure of votes, cheap popularity, or political gains” must not overpower prudence and goodwill.Earlier in the address, he specifically urged government officials implementing campaigns and policies to be courteous and considerate, and to respect citizens' dignity. “Experience shows that it is neither the government alone that can resolve all the problems of society, nor is it true that problems can be resolved only through agitations,” he said, advocating dialogue and community participation.That theme opened into the RSS's post-centenary plans. Bhagwat said Swayamsevaks would work to bring together organisations combating drug addiction and build nationwide resistance to what he called a “serious national problem”. He also urged the government to consider restrictions on OTT platforms, while asking families to teach young people to distinguish appropriate from inappropriate digital content.Although concerns over drugs and digital content had figured in his 2024 address too, the proposed nationwide mobilisation gave the anti-drug initiative a more specific organisational direction.In education, he cited observations from around 1,296 rural schools across 210 districts in 21 Sangh organisational regions, claiming improvements in attendance, learning and parental involvement where Swayamsevaks and villagers cooperated. No underlying methodology was disclosed in the speech.Bhagwat said centenary outreach had covered over 10 crore households in 4.61 lakh villages and 41,076 urban localities. Contacts at home and abroad would continue, he indicated. The organisation's five initiatives — social harmony, family awareness, environment, self-awareness and Swadeshi, and civic discipline — were “not merely programs to be undertaken for a year”, but intended to change everyday conduct.On identity, Bhagwat said the Hindu worldview prescribed no particular form of worship, food habit, language or caste, and called for acceptance of diversity within shared national belonging. He also advocated singing 'Vande Mataram' in full, entering a dispute in which Congress has reaffirmed its decision to sing only the first two stanzas at party events.The address thus combined a familiar warning about alleged external interference with a stronger appeal for constitutional restraint and a continuing society-led role for the RSS beyond its centenary.
Article Summary: Mohan Bhagwat linked political protests and distrust of institutions to alleged foreign attempts to destabilise the country. But his Vijayadashami address in Nagpur also carried a message for governments: respect citizens' dignity, act within constitutional limits and avoid deepening divisions.

Article Title: 'Highly inspiring': PM Modi hails Mohan Bhagwat's speech on RSS Sthapana Divas

During the RSS centenary celebrations in Nagpur, Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised Mohan Bhagwat's impactful speech.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday praised Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh RSS ) chief Mohan Bhagwat ’s speech at the organisation’s centenary Vijayadashami celebrations in Nagpur, noting his focus on national development, social harmony, self-reliance and nation-building.Describing the address as “very motivating”, PM Modi said Bhagwat had covered several important subjects, including the need to strengthen society and promote self-reliance.In a post on X, the prime minister also highlighted Bhagwat’s remarks on the spirit of service and nation-building among RSS volunteers, along with the organisation’s initiative known as panch parivartan.“Particularly noteworthy was his emphasis on the commitment to Seva and nation building that is integral to every RSS Swayamsevak. He also spoke about the panch parivartan and how these can contribute meaningfully to positive social change,” PM Modi wrote.The RSS marked its centenary Vijayadashami celebrations at Reshimbagh Ground in Nagpur, bringing its year-long commemorative programme towards its conclusion.Addressing the gathering, Bhagwat remembered Sant Ravidas, Swami Shraddhanand and Swami Lakshmanananda Saraswati, highlighting their contributions to spiritual devotion, social harmony and the preservation of religious values.He said the organisation had spent the past century seeking to awaken self-awareness and strengthen India’s unity and identity.“Remembering them is also appropriate because the work that the Sangh has been carrying out for the past 100 years is precisely aimed at awakening this self-awareness. On the foundation of that self-awareness, identity, and ethos, it strives to make India united and strong,” Bhagwat said.Bhagwat also discussed Panch Parivartan, highlighting self-awareness and the adoption of Swadeshi as key elements of the initiative.Referring to the concept, he said self-awareness was reflected in the Preamble to the Indian Constitution, particularly its opening words, “We, the people of India”.“As our Prant Sanghchalak ji mentioned in his introductory remarks regarding panch parivartan, one of its key aspects is practising self-awareness and adoption of Swadeshi. This self-awareness is reflected in the preamble of our Constitution, where we refer to ourselves as 'We, the people of India',” he said.The RSS was founded in Nagpur by Keshav Hedgewar, its first Sarsanghchalak, on Vijayadashami in 1925. The organisation has observed the festival annually since its establishment.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million mansion faces new developments as officials schedule another property review
Article Text:
Travis Kelce mansion (Getty Images)

Travis Kelce’s Ohio mansion draws attention over privacy plans

Travis Kelce’s landscaping proposal faces fresh questions
