Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion offers the privacy and luxury expected of an NFL star, but making the estate more secluded has proved complicated. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end now faces questions from local residents about landscaping, aging sewer lines and the impact of new barriers on the neighborhood. What began as an effort to improve the property has turned into a wider discussion about balancing personal space with community concerns. With another review scheduled for November, Kelce’s plans for his historic lakeside home remain partly unresolved, despite progress on one major renovation proposal.Travis Kelce purchased the 3.5-acre Bratenahl estate on March 2, 2026, for $5.35 million. Located along Lake Erie near Cleveland, the property stands out for its scale, history and impressive facilities.Known as Moyenage, the mansion dates back to 1904. The historic residence spans 21,140 square feet and features eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, seven fireplaces, a sauna, a fitness centre and a heated outdoor pool. Its grounds also include a five-car garage and a guest cottage created from a former gatehouse.However, improving security around such a large property comes with challenges. Kelce’s proposed fencing initially included an eight-foot barrier, prompting concerns from nearby homeowners about lake views and the appearance of the neighborhood.The revised design received unanimous approval from Bratenahl’s Architectural Review Board on September 8. The plan calls for a six-foot black aluminium fence covering approximately 1,190 linear feet, with matching gates and a design intended to complement existing stone walls.Contractor Jacob Kutz explained that the changes addressed residents’ objections, including concerns about preserving views of Lake Erie. The fence will also sit about two feet inside the property boundary to avoid interfering with shared sewer infrastructure.Although the fence has received approval, the mansion’s landscaping plans have encountered further delays. During an October 6 meeting, village officials examined a proposal to plant evergreen trees behind the property.Residents raised concerns about the trees’ eventual height and their possible impact on neighboring homes. Officials indicated that plants growing below 10 feet could offer privacy without creating the same problems. The board approved the front-yard landscaping but postponed its decision on the rear section.Shared utilities have also become a point of contention. Neighbor Katherine Bolton warned that roots from roughly 50 proposed evergreens could damage an aging sewer line reportedly shared with the estate. She said protecting her section of the pipe could cost $75,000.Travis Kelce’s representatives have discussed a $7,500 repair to part of the shared sewer, and the fence design includes access gates for maintenance crews.Bratenahl’s Architectural Review Board plans to reconsider the landscaping proposal on November 10, 2026. Until then, Kelce’s efforts to improve privacy at Moyenage remain subject to local review and the concerns of those living nearby.
Article Summary: Travis Kelce purchased the 3.5-acre Bratenahl estate on March 2, 2026, for $5.35 million. Located along Lake Erie near Cleveland, the mansion dates back to 1904. The historic residence spans 21,140 square feet and features eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, seven fireplaces, a sauna, a fitness centre and a heated outdoor pool.

Article Title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf lost $3 million on $23 million Tiburon mansion after four years of searching for a buyer
Article Text:
Steffi Graf-Andre Agassi (Getty Images)

Andre Agassi's Tiburon estate took years to sell

Why the luxury home struggled to attract buyers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In 2006, tennis legends Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf made a costly decision involving one of their most impressive real estate assets. After nearly four years on the market, the couple finally found a buyer for their sprawling Tiburon estate in California. The property attracted attention for its breathtaking views, luxury features and celebrity connections. Yet the final sale price came in below what Agassi had paid five years earlier. The deal showed that even a high-end property in a sought-after location can struggle to find the right buyer when its upkeep and price become difficult to justify.Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf agreed to sell the 3.5-acre estate for $20 million, around $3 million less than the $23 million Agassi reportedly paid in 2001. The sale was expected to close in the first week of January 2007, according to Bill Bullock, whose firm represented the couple.The property offered plenty of space and privacy. It featured a 10,500-square-foot main house, separate staff quarters measuring 2,500 square feet, two swimming pools, a stream and a tennis court. Its elevated setting also provided views of the Golden Gate Bridge and the San Francisco skyline.However, the estate's size came with significant carrying costs. Agassi's family rarely used the property, and his financial advisers wanted him to sell it rather than continue paying to maintain a largely vacant home.The original asking price stood at $24.5 million. After several reductions, Agassi lowered it to $21 million about six months before the reported deal. Bullock explained why the couple became more flexible on price."When they considered the annual cost of that property to sit there vacant, they decided that they needed a little inducement for the marketplace and they started reducing the price,"The final $20 million offer still ranked among the Bay Area's most expensive home sales that year. Stuart Peterson, president of hedge fund Artis Capital Management, agreed to buy the estate. His fund had also been a major investor in YouTube before Google's $1.65 billion acquisition of the video-sharing company.Despite its impressive setting, the Tiburon property had a drawback. Built in 1976, the house had not received a major renovation since the mid-1990s. That left parts of the estate feeling dated to prospective buyers, making it harder to compete in the luxury market.Bullock said several wealthy visitors, including movie stars, had toured the home but ultimately passed on it. The buyer planned to make changes, although details were not disclosed before the transaction closed.Andre Agassi had wanted the property for years. He first considered buying it in the mid-1990s while married to actress Brooke Shields, but she disliked the compound and discouraged the purchase. When it returned to the market, Agassi acted quickly rather than risk losing it again.By 2006, Agassi had retired from professional tennis and was living in Las Vegas with Graf and their two children. The couple were also exploring property development, including a luxury condo-hotel project in Idaho. Their Tiburon sale marked a shift away from a costly home they seldom used, even as they pursued new opportunities in real estate.
Article Summary: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf agreed to sell the 3.5-acre estate for $20 million. The sale was expected to close in the first week of January 2007. The property featured a 10,500-square-foot main house, separate staff quarters and two swimming pools.

Article Title: 'Pay the community a dividend': Trump's message to companies building massive data centres
Article Text:
Trump asks data centres to generate their own electricity, offer community dividends

Trump warns data centres could move to China

US President Donald Trump has said new and large data centres should generate their own electricity and supply or sell surplus power to local communities or the grid, arguing that the move could help prevent electricity price increases. He also urged companies to offer financial benefits to communities hosting data centres, saying such arrangements could make projects more popular with residents.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he had been closely monitoring data centres and concluded that new facilities, including very large ones, should be required to produce their own electricity. He argued that supplying surplus power to the local community or grid could potentially lead to lower electricity prices."As the President of the United States, I have been watching Data Centers very closely, and have come to a very strong conclusion. New and large, in some cases gigantic, Data enters are mandated by me to make their own electricity, and give or sell any excess back to the local community, or grid, and therefore there is electric price increase. In fact, there could be a substantial decrease. Other elements likewise! If companies want to make their Data Centers popular, pay the community, and/or individuals within the community, a “dividend.” I have watched the process closely, and Data Centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck. MAKE DEALS, and get them built!!!"Trump also suggested that companies could pay a dividend to local communities or individuals living near data centre projects. He said financial arrangements had helped turn opposition to some facilities into public support.The remarks come amid growing scrutiny of data centres because of their electricity requirements and their potential impact on local power costs.Trump has previously defended the rapid expansion of data centres in the US, warning that blocking projects could give China an advantage in the global race for artificial intelligence.During a rally outside Dayton, Ohio, ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, Trump said data centres could bring economic benefits to local communities and urged voters not to oppose their development.Also read - ‘There’s so much money to be made’: Trump defends US data centres, warns they could go to China “There’s so much money to be made for Ohio. You can’t just turn them off. They’ll go to China,” Trump told supporters, according to the New York Post.Trump also linked the expansion of data centres to competition with China in artificial intelligence, claiming the US was ahead in what he called “superintelligence”.“We’re beating China,” he said, arguing that the US should continue developing its AI infrastructure rather than turn away data centre projects.At the same time, Trump backed legislation promoted by Republican Senator Jon Husted that aims to prevent data centres from raising electricity costs for other consumers and require facilities to cover expenses associated with their power use. Trump said he would sign the proposed Ratepayer Protection Act into law “immediately within 24 hours” if Republicans retained control.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump says new data centres should generate their own electricity and sell surplus power to local communities or the grid. He also urged companies to offer financial benefits to communities hosting data centres. Trump has previously defended the rapid expansion of data centres in the US, warning that blocking projects could give China an advantage.

Article Title: A Bhopal merchant invested Rs 35,000 in a 1917 British war loan, 109 years later, UK’s Debt Management Office says it finds no evidence the loan was ever its obligation
Article Text:
The Ruthiya family had sought repayment of the Rs 35,000 subscription made to Indian War Loan.

Poll Vote & Share your view Is there a need for transparency regarding historical financial records from colonial times? Yes, absolutely Only if it impacts current claims 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BHOPAL: The UK’s Debt Management Office (DMO) has said it can find no evidence that a 109-year-old Indian War Loan, in which a Bhopal merchant invested Rs 35,000 in 1917, was or is an obligation of British govt, leaving a Madhya Pradesh family’s claim unresolved. The office did not say whether the money was repaid.“We have investigated and can find no evidence that the loan you refer to was or is an obligation of the UK govt,” DMO said in an email dated Oct 16.It was replying to Shreyansh Raniwala, legal counsel for the family of Vivek Ruthiya (63) of Sehore.Although the email is not a judicial finding on the family’s claim, and DMO has not acknowledged any outstanding debt, the reply has drawn a sharp reaction from social activist Vinay Ruthiya, who asked why the British authorities had given no account of the loan’s repayment or settlement.Ruthiya said the family had authenticated the available records and sent them through its counsel. He argued that British govt should clarify whether the subscription appears in historical financial records and, if so, how the liability was accounted for.“If the loan was repaid, there should be a record showing when and how it was settled. We submitted the documents they asked for, including the historical certificate.We want a clear answer on what happened to the money,” he said.The family had sought repayment of the Rs 35,000 subscription made to Indian War Loan. It maintains that the amount was never repaid and has been seeking an official account of what became of the investment.The claim rests on a certificate dated June 4, 1917. It records the subscription by Seth Jumma Lal Ruthia of the firm Seth Rama Kishan Jaskaran Ruthia, in the princely state of Bhopal, and bears the signature of W S Davis, then political agent in Bhopal.According to the family, the instrument carried interest at 5.5%, and the certificate has remained among its papers for more than a century.Seth Jumma Lal Ruthia died in 1937, a decade before British rule in India ended.The certificate gives the family a documentary basis for its claim. By itself, however, it does not prove that a debt remains outstanding or that present-day UK govt is legally liable for it. The family estimates that the original sum, compounded at 5.5% a year for 109 years, could run to several crores of rupees today.A calculation based on the rise in gold prices, it suggests, could exceed Rs 10 crore.War loans in British India were govt-issued debt instruments floated to raise funds from the public to finance military expenditure, especially during World War I.Marketed as patriotic investments, they encouraged citizens, traders and institutions to lend money to colonial govt for war efforts including military supplies and troop payments in return for fixed interest.During the British era, a political agent was a key administrative and diplomatic representative of the Crown in princely states.These officers managed relations with local rulers, supervised governance matters and ensured alignment with British authority. Historians also note that W S Davis, who had signed the bond certificate, had literary associations in Bhopal.He apparently had translated Hayat-i-Qudsi: Life of the Nawab Gauhar Begum, a biography written by Sultan Jahan Begum and published in 1918.
Article Summary: The Ruthiya family had sought repayment of the Rs 35,000 subscription made to Indian War Loan. The family estimates that the original sum, compounded at 5.5% a year for 109 years, could run to several crores of rupees today. A calculation based on the rise in gold prices, it suggests, could exceed Rs 10 crore.

Article Title: An Ahmedabad family spent Rs 2.2 lakh buying clothes in Singapore after Air India left their luggage behind; 11 years later, consumer commission orders airline to pay Rs 2.5 lakh
Article Text:
An Ahmedabad family experienced significant distress when Air India failed to load their luggage during a trip. (File pic)





AHMEDABAD: An Ahmedabad family spent Rs 2.2 lakh buying clothes and other essentials in Singapore after Air India allegedly left their luggage behind at Ahmedabad airport in January 2015.Eleven years later, a consumer commission has ordered the airline to reimburse Rs 1.5 lakh of the expenses and pay an additional Rs 1 lakh in compensation for deficiency in service.The Gujarat State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission passed the order in an appeal filed by Dayal Wadhwani, a resident of Bhat, who travelled to Singapore with four family members for a seven-day holiday.On reaching Singapore airport, the family waited for their checked-in luggage but was eventually informed that the bags had not been loaded onto their flight from Ahmedabad. They were told the luggage would arrive on the next flight that evening. However, the bags never arrived during the entire trip.With their belongings unavailable, the family had to buy clothes and other essentials, spending 4,439 Singapore dollars, equivalent to around Rs 2.2 lakh at the time.After returning to India, Wadhwani sent a legal notice to Air India. When the airline did not respond, he approached the Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Ahmedabad, which awarded him Rs 1 lakh in compensation but rejected his claim for reimbursement of the shopping expenses.The commission reasoned that the family had brought the purchased clothes back to India and continued using them.Wadhwani challenged the decision before the state commission, arguing that the purchases had been necessitated by the airline's failure to deliver the luggage.Air India opposed the appeal, contending that the family should hand over the purchased articles to the airline if it wanted reimbursement, to prevent unjust enrichment or double benefit.The state commission rejected this argument, observing that missing baggage deprives travellers not only of essential belongings but also of items intended for their holiday.“If the luggage containing such articles does not reach the destination, a traveller is deprived not only of essential belongings but also of articles intended for enjoyment and recreation. Consequently, the non-availability of such articles can materially affect the traveller’s ability to enjoy the holiday as planned,” it observed.The commission said purchases made under such circumstances could not be treated as ordinary holiday shopping, as travellers might not get items in their preferred colour, size, design or style. It added that the unexpected expenditure could also reduce the money available for planned activities such as sightseeing and recreation.While allowing reimbursement, the commission deducted 25% of the shopping bill because the family had continued using the clothes after returning to India. It also deducted 375 Singapore dollars already paid by Air India, bringing the reimbursement amount to Rs 1.5 lakh.The airline was additionally directed to pay Rs 1 lakh in compensation for deficiency in service.
Article Summary: Dayal Wadhwani travelled to Singapore with four family members for a seven-day holiday in January 2015. The family waited for their checked-in luggage but was eventually informed that the bags had not been loaded onto their flight from Ahmedabad. They were told the luggage would arrive on the next flight that evening. However, the bags never arrived during the entire trip. With their belongings unavailable, the family had to buy clothes and other essentials.

Article Title: India and Australia hold joint wargames as China becomes more assertive in the Indo-Pacific
Article Text:
An Indian and an Australian soldier during Exercise AUSTRAHIND 2025 near Perth. (Image credit: Indian Army)

Su-57 For India? Why Russia Is Watching China’s J-35 Moves And Pakistan’s Stealth Ambitions Closely

India and Australia have begun the fifth edition of their joint army exercise AUSTRAHIND at the Foreign Training Node in Thiruvananthapuram, as the two countries widen cooperation in maritime security, interoperability and defence industry. The exercise started on Monday, October 19th to November 1st. About 120 personnel from each army are taking part, with the Indian contingent drawn from the Garhwal Rifles along with other arms and services and the Australian side from its 13 Brigade. A New Zealand observer delegation is attending for the first time. The previous edition was held at Irwin Barracks in Perth from October 2025.The theme is joint sub-conventional operations in island and coastal environments under Chapter VII of the UN mandate. Troops will carry out joint planning, tactical drills and combat-oriented training with aerial and maritime elements, covering surveillance and reconnaissance, protection of vital installations and disaster relief contingencies. The Ministry of Defence says the aim is better interoperability and a shared understanding of tactics and procedures in island and coastal terrain.The army exercise sits within a wider set of engagements. AUSINDEX is the bilateral naval exercise, Malabar brings in Japan and the United States, and Australia hosts the Pitch Black air exercise and Talisman Sabre, in which India took part for the first time in 2025.At the second Defence Ministers' Dialogue, the two sides said they looked forward to India's enhanced participation in Talisman Sabre 2027.Practical arrangements have kept pace. The Comprehensive Strategic Partnership was announced in June 2020 along with the Mutual Logistics Support Arrangement. In November 2024, the two air forces signed an arrangement at Air Staff Talks in New Delhi that lets Australian KC-30 tankers refuel Indian military aircraft, a first step towards refuelling the Navy's P-8I aircraft.The dialogue between the two governments has also become regular. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Australia's Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles held the first Defence Ministers' Dialogue in Canberra on October 9, 2025, where they signed an agreement on information sharing, a memorandum on submarine search and rescue cooperation, and terms of reference for Joint Staff Talks. The 10th Defence Policy Talks followed in New Delhi on May 8, 2026, led by Joint Secretary Amitabh Prasad and Australia's First Assistant Secretary Bernard Philip, and reviewed maritime cooperation, interoperability and defence industry links. The two ministers met again at the second dialogue in New Delhi on June 1, 2026, reviewing progress on a Joint Maritime Security Collaboration Roadmap, agreeing to begin work on a memorandum on defence articles and services, and committing to continued aircraft deployments from each other's territory. The first Joint Staff Talks are still expected later this year.
Article Summary: India and Australia have begun the fifth edition of their joint army exercise AUSTRAHIND at the Foreign Training Node in Thiruvananthapuram. The theme is joint sub-conventional operations in island and coastal environments under Chapter VII of the UN mandate. About 120 personnel from each army are taking part, with the Indian contingent drawn from the Garhwal Rifles.

Article Title: Sugar stocks tumble today: Bajaj Hindusthan, Renuka Sugars plunge up to 5%; here's why
Article Text:
Sugar stocks slip after govt's latest ethanol procurement tender

Oil firms drop sugar-based ethanol from 2026-27 tender

Grain-based ethanol takes centre stage

Sugar supply concerns behind the move

NEW DELHI: Sugar stocks turned sour on Monday, tumbling over 5% after the government halted sugar-based ethanol supplies for 2026-27.Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar led the losses among the listed companies, with its shares falling 5.22% to Rs 20.16 on the Bombay Stock Exchange in early trade. Dwarikesh Sugar Industries declined 4.45% to Rs 44.28, while Shree Renuka Sugars dropped 4.43% to Rs 21.16. Dalmia Bharat Sugar and Industries slipped 3.24% to Rs 466, Dhampur Sugar Mills fell 2.81% to Rs 191.90 and Balrampur Chini Mills lost 2.55% to Rs 704.35. EID Parry India was down 1.57% at Rs 683.75 on the BSE.The sell-off came after the latest ethanol procurement tender barred supplies made from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses. For sugar mills, the decision shuts the door on an important outlet for their produce, particularly one that offers higher margins.Dalal Street also started the week on a weak note, with the BSE Sensex slipping 307.63 points, or 0.41%, to 74,421.64, while the Nifty 50 fell 81.30 points, or 0.35%, to 23,096.80.The government has directed oil marketing companies (OMCs) to bring sugar diversion for ethanol production down to zero during the 2026-27 supply year.The restriction was set out in a tender issued by Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) on October 16 on behalf of state-run OMCs. "The Government of India has issued directions that sugar diversion for ethanol be reduced to zero for ethanol supply year 2026-27," the tender document said, as cited by PTI.It further stated, "No offers have been sought for ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar or sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses in this quantity bid tender."The tender seeks bids for around 11 billion litres of ethanol for the period from November 2026 to October 2027. The volume is intended to meet the requirement of blending 20% ethanol with petrol under the nationwide programme.With sugar-based feedstocks excluded, the tender allows producers to offer ethanol made from maize, broken rice, surplus rice procured by the Food Corporation of India (FCI) and C-heavy molasses.However, the shift does not come with a higher incentive for maize-based ethanol. The procurement price has been reduced to Rs 68.86 per litre from Rs 71.86, while the incentive has been cut to Rs 2.79 per litre from Rs 5.79. The lower rates are expected to reduce returns for producers supplying ethanol made from maize.The changes reshape the feedstock options available to distilleries participating in the petrol-blending programme, which has so far drawn on both grain-based and sugarcane-based ethanol.The decision comes at a time when domestic sugar availability is under pressure from concerns over production. Poor rainfall in key sugar-producing states, including Maharashtra and Karnataka, has raised the risk of lower output, alongside concerns about rising prices.India, the world's largest sugar consumer, has expanded ethanol blending to reduce its reliance on imported crude oil. But the use of sugarcane and sugar for fuel also competes with the quantity available for domestic consumption, particularly when production is constrained.The latest tender seeks to balance these competing requirements: maintaining adequate sugar supplies and containing domestic prices while continuing the country's petrol-blending programme.India has adopted petrol containing up to 20% ethanol, known as E20, as the nationwide standard. Ethanol is produced from agricultural raw materials, including sugarcane and grains, and blended with petrol to replace part of fossil fuel consumption.The programme has opened up a substantial market for domestic distilleries and provided farmers with an additional source of demand for agricultural produce.For the 2026-27 supply cycle, however, the exclusion of sugar-based ethanol puts greater emphasis on alternative feedstocks. The availability of grain, procurement prices and distillery capacity will be important factors in meeting the programme's blending requirements.
Article Summary: Government halts sugar-based ethanol supplies for 2026-27. Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar leads the losses among the listed companies. BSE Sensex slips 307.63 points, or 0.41%, to 74,421.64.

Article Title: Bombay HC to hear on October 26 plea filed by actor Imran Khan against 'Leave India' order
Article Text:
The B​ombay High Court will hear the petition on October 26, as Imran Khan faces a departure deadline

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the government provide clearer criteria for issuing leave notices to foreign nationals? Absolutely, transparency is crucial. Not necessary, the system works as is. Maybe, but only if it changes often. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





MUMBAI: Bombay high court on Monday said it will hear on October 26, actor Imran Khan Pal’s petition against a ‘leave India notice’ issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer, (FRRO), Mumbai, to him on October 14, four days after a protest where he was detained. The notice requires him to leave the country, as a US national, by October 28.The HC asked the actor to also make State a party.Senior counsel Venkatesh Dhond for the actor mentioned the matter for urgent hearing. He said, “ this is a petition where a person who has been residing in India since he was 2 years old, is asked to leave without notice, without any hearing, without reasons…”.The actor has no criminal antecedents, Dhond said to a query. He said the petition mentions that he has no criminal record and no antecedents.The Chief Justice led bench before which the matter was mentioned asked if all parties were served a copy of the petition. Dhond said it was. The Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh for the Centre and FRRO, a central authority under the Bureau of Immigration said he received a copy of the petition “10 minutes ago.”Dhond sought a hearing the day after. Singh said it can be heard on October 26.Dhond said since the actor has been asked to leave by October 28 it would be cutting it too close. However, Singh said, “we will come prepared to argue the matter.”The actor, almost 44, had filed the petition on Saturday challenging the notice as “arbitrary, unreasoned and wholly misconceived’’ and against principles of natural justice.The notice flouts his fundamental rights to equality under Article 14 and to life under article 21 of the Indian constitution, his lawyers contended.On Saturday the actor also was issued a fresh notice this time a show cause notice on why his Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) status should not be cancelled by invoking a provision under the Citizenship Act that says for any action violatingArticles 14 and 21 are constitutional guarantees available to even foreigners in India, it underscored. He was given no reasons nor any reasonable opportunity to be heard and the notice was issued directly, the petition argued.The FRRO, had within four days of a protest in Mumbai against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, where the actor was present, invoked the Immigration and Foreigners Act (IFA) 2025 to issue him the departure notice on October 14. The notice is based on “purported contravention of uncited provisions of the IFA and the Rules and Orders’’ under it.His petition says , Merely …mechanically reproducing the words of a statutory provision is not sufficient in law and cannot be countenanced” It take a ground that the actor “who has lived in India for forty-two years, is apparently sought to be expelled solely because an FIR has been registered. The FIR is at the stage of investigation.The offences alleged under Sections 223, 126(2), 189(2), 189(3) and 189(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 are all bailable, and none carries a punishment exceeding two years. No charge-sheet has been filed, no court has taken cognizance, and no charge has been framed.Even if a charge-sheet were to befiled, the Court may decline to take cognizance. If it takes cognizance, the Petitioner may be discharged. If charges are framed, he may be acquitted.To expel the Petitioner at the very threshold of that process is to visit the ultimate consequence upon a mere allegation and to condemn him, in effect, on the mere recording by the police of an intimation of the commission of an offence.”The urgent interim relief the actor will argue for next Monday is a stay of the notice and final relief is to quash and set it aside.
Article Summary: Bombay high court will hear actor Imran Khan Pal’s petition against a ‘leave India notice’ issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer, (FRRO), Mumbai, to him on October 14. The notice requires him to leave the country, as a US national, by October 28.

Gold price prediction

Article Title: 'Geography is real': Rubio says India-US trade deal close, explains Trump admin's stance on Russian oil
Article Text:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio

Why the US is taking another look at Russian oil sanctions

Graham bill and geopolitics

NEW DELHI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Monday said that India and the US are close to finalising a trade deal. He also explained the reason behind Washington's consideration of India energy needs before imposing sanctions or tariffs linked to Russian oil.Speaking to reporters in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, Rubio said the US had waived some sanctions in recent months to limit their impact on global energy supplies and prices."We've had to waive sanctions over the past few months because of the impact on global supplies and prices...We have to manage all of these things.”Explaining how Washington was balancing trade negotiations with India and decisions on sanctions, Rubio said countries had to consider several factors when making foreign policy decisions, including how easily they could access alternative energy sources.“We're trying to finalise a trade deal with India right now. We're very close to doing that. That's one of the things we taken into consideration when the President makes a decision about national security waivers and things of that nature. Every country has a complex set of factors that it has to take into account. Geography is real. For some countries, it's very difficult to acquire energy from alternative sources.That's not an excuse, but all of that has to be balanced when making foreign policy..."Rubio is currently in Uzbekistan and is scheduled to visit Mumbai on Tuesday to meet external affairs minister S Jaishankar. He will also travel to Jamnagar later in the week, which is home to one of the world's largest refineries.Rubio's remarks come after US President Donald Trump waived several sanctions related to Russian fuel sales that were due to take effect under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.The law, which has now been paused, would have allowed the US to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods imported from the five largest buyers of Russian crude oil or natural gas. India and China are among these countries.Rubio said the proposed measures would affect not just Russia but also countries that buy its energy. The US wants to use a 60-day period to study how the sanctions and tariffs could affect the global economy and its own economy."These sanctions were not just sanctions on Russia. They include tariffs on a number of countries—India, for example, and others. And so I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the U.S. economy," Rubio said.He said India had diversified its energy sources but still bought a significant amount of energy from Russia. Switching to other suppliers immediately was not easy, he added."You've got countries like India, for example, that have voluntarily diversified their energy portfolio, but are still getting a substantial amount of energy from Russia because it's hard to pivot from one day to the next. But they're also an important ally and partner of the United States. So we need that period of time to sort of study all this and figure out what the right combination is," he added.Rubio also said the US was considering changes in the global situation since the Graham bill was passed. He pointed to the growing conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi militia, along with the war between Russia and Ukraine.He said global energy supplies were under pressure because of several factors, including Iran, the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and damage to energy infrastructure during the Russia-Ukraine war."I think when the bill was passed, one of the reasons the waivers were put in there is understanding that they would need some period of time to study this, given all the different things that are that are going on in the world right now, including the pressure on global energy supplies that are happening not just because of Iran and not just because of the Straits of Hormuz, but increasingly because of the Houthis attacking Saudi Arabia, and because of the war with Ukraine and Russia, where energy infrastructure is being hit, and so that's having an impact on global prices as well," he said.Meanwhile, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal last week said that the first part of the agreement had been finalised and had moved to the legal drafting stage. "US bilateral trade agreement's first tranche has been finalised and it is going through final contours, the legal drafting and we hope to be able to finalise that soon and operationalise that once we get the competitive advantage over our peer countries," Goyal said.
Article Summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio says India and the US are close to finalising a trade deal. He also explained the reason behind Washington's consideration of India energy needs before imposing sanctions or tariffs linked to Russian oil. Rubio is currently in Uzbekistan and is scheduled to visit Mumbai on Tuesday.

Article Title: Stock market crash today: Sensex ends over 870 points down, Nifty50 below 22,900 - top reasons for fall
Article Text:
Shares of major private sector lenders, particularly Axis Bank and HDFC Bank, led the losses on the benchmark indices.

Stock market crash today

:

Why did stock market crash today?

Banking stocks down

Foreign investor outflows continue to weigh on sentiment

Crude oil prices high

Weakness across global markets

Investors book profits after recent gains

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

After a week of rallying, the Indian equity benchmarks crashed in trade on Monday. Heavy selling in major private banking stocks, along with other factors, weighed on investor sentiment and pulled the benchmark indices into negative territory. Nifty50 ended the day at 22,888.95, down 257 points or 1.11%. BSE Sensex closed at 73,852.90, down 876 points or 1.17%. The decline provisionally erased nearly Rs 4.70 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies, taking it down to Rs 467 lakh crore.V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited said, “The momentum created by the 2.8% surge in Nifty last week and the good results from the banking majors after the better-than-expected results from the leading IT companies have the potential to keep the market resilient. However, the escalation of the tensions in Hormuz and the consequent surge in Brent crude to $109 will act as a strong headwind to the market. ”“Even though the attractive valuations of the large-caps and the appreciation of the rupee have turned the stance of FIIs towards India a bit positive, it is unlikely to sustain, given the high crude price. Large-caps outperforming the mid-and small-caps is a rational trend, and this is likely to sustain, going forward.The market actions this week are likely to be stock-specific in response to the Q2 results,” he added.Axis Bank was the biggest loser on the Sensex , with its shares falling around 5%. HDFC Bank, Infosys, Trent, HUL, Bajaj Finserv, NTPC, Bajaj Finance and ICICI Bank also declined by up to 2%. Adani Ports and Maruti Suzuki moved against the broader trend, gaining as much as 2%.Selling pressure extended to the broader market as well.Shares of major private sector lenders, particularly Axis Bank and HDFC Bank, led the losses on the benchmark indices after their second-quarter results failed to meet market expectations.Axis Bank shares dropped more than 5% after the lender reported a 38% year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 7,003 crore for the second quarter of FY27. Despite the growth in earnings, the result fell short of analysts' estimates.HDFC Bank also faced selling pressure, with its shares declining more than 2%. The country's largest private sector lender reported a net profit of Rs 19,510 crore for Q2FY27, up 4.6% from Rs 18,641 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.Shares of ICICI Bank and Yes Bank also came under pressure, falling by more than 1% each.Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought Indian equities worth Rs 1,166 crore on Friday, according to provisional data from the NSE. However, the purchase was relatively small compared with the substantial outflows recorded during October.FIIs have been net sellers in nine of the 11 trading sessions so far this month, keeping sustained pressure on the domestic equity market.Brent crude futures fell by more than 2%, but continued to trade well above last week's levels at over $107 per barrel. Meanwhile, US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude was hovering close to $100 per barrel.The decline in oil prices followed US President Donald Trump's decision to waive sweeping sanctions on Russia, including restrictions targeting its energy sector. However, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump would take up to 60 days to evaluate the economic consequences of the waiver.Indian equities followed the broader decline across several international markets. Japan's Nikkei slipped 0.64%, while Indonesia's Jakarta Composite plunged more than 5%. South Korea's Kospi moved in the opposite direction, rising around 2% as investors bought AI stocks after their recent decline.Indian equities are seen as having an anti-AI advantage. As a result, gains in AI-related stocks can sometimes coincide with weakness in the domestic market.US markets also suffered a sharp sell-off on Friday. The technology-heavy Nasdaq tumbled more than 2%, while the S&P 500 declined by over 1%.Monday's decline came after Indian markets had rallied sharply over the previous two trading sessions. The Nifty gained more than 2% on Thursday and Friday despite several headwinds, prompting investors to lock in some of their recent profits.Market participants were also bracing for possible volatility around the Nifty's expiry ahead of Tuesday's market holiday.Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments Limited said, “Indian equities came under renewed selling pressure, reversing the recent recovery as weak global cues and selling in private banks and IT stocks weighed on investor sentiment. Global markets remained cautious ahead of a busy week of corporate earnings. Private banks remained under pressure following quarterly earnings and concerns over margin trends, while PSU banks bucked the broader weakness, supported by expectations of relatively resilient margins and asset quality. ”“Crude oil prices eased after the US waived key sanctions linked to Russia, raising expectations of increased Russian fuel supplies to the global market. However, crude prices remained elevated, with geopolitical tensions continuing to influence the outlook. The Nifty slipped below the psychologically important 23,000 level, while broader market breadth remained weak, reflecting cautious investor sentiment amid earnings-related volatility and uncertain global cues,” he added.
Article Summary: BSE Sensex closed at 73,852.90, down 876 points or 1.17%. The decline provisionally erased nearly Rs 4.70 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies. Major private sector lenders, particularly Axis Bank and HDFC Bank, led the losses on the benchmark indices.

Article Title: Kospi hits the brakes: South Korean benchmark plunges 7.5%, triggers 'sidecar' stop for investors
Article Text:
Kospi tumbles over 7% as tech stocks lose steam

Samsung, SK Hynix lead South Korean market rout

‘Sidecar’ triggered

South Korea’s stock market hit a rough patch on Thursday, with the benchmark Kospi plunging 7.49% as technology stocks came under heavy selling pressure. The rout spread across Asian markets, prompting the country’s exchange operator to trigger a five-minute trading halt on programme sell orders after a sharp drop in index futures.The KOSPI dropped 450.02 points to 5,558.79, putting it on course for a seventh consecutive session of losses, its longest losing streak since September 2024. The index has fallen nearly 35% from its record high in June.The pressure on Asian equities followed a technology-led sell-off on Wall Street after US consumer price inflation accelerated more than expected in September. The data fuelled concerns that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates later this year, putting technology companies and AI-related stocks under further pressure.MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell 3.3%, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 4.8%. S&P 500 e-mini futures were down 0.5%.Major technology companies accounted for some of the steepest losses on the South Korean exchange. Samsung Electronics shares fell 9.05%, while SK Hynix dropped 11.06%, reflecting the broader weakness across Asia’s semiconductor supply chain.Battery maker LG Energy Solution lost 3.44%. Hyundai Motor declined 3.99%, while sister automaker Kia Corp fell 2.03%.The selling extended to other Asian technology companies. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) fell 2%, while Japan’s memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings plunged more than 11%. SoftBank Group, an investor in AI, declined 9.4%.Market breadth in South Korea remained heavily negative. Of the 889 stocks traded, 768 declined and 90 advanced. Foreign investors sold shares worth a net 355.6 billion won.The won, meanwhile, strengthened 0.21% to 1,339.5 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform, compared with its previous close of 1,342.3.The sharp decline prompted the South Korean exchange operator to activate a sell-side “sidecar”, an automatic mechanism designed to temporarily cool trading during periods of heavy selling. The measure suspends program sell orders for five minutes after steep losses in index futures.The trigger came as the KOSPI extended its decline to seven consecutive sessions. The benchmark has now shed nearly 35% since its June record, with retail investors among those hit hardest during a sell-off in July, when the index fell around 20%. Losses in highly leveraged single-stock exchange-traded funds (ETFs) contributed to the damage during that period.The sell-off in Asia followed Wall Street’s third consecutive session of losses. The S&P 500 declined 1.1% overnight, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.9%. A gauge of semiconductor stocks recorded its sixth straight day of losses as investors reassessed the outlook for companies sensitive to borrowing costs.Meanwhile, in South Korea’s bond market, December futures on three-year treasury bonds rose 0.12 point to 103.00. The yield on the most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond fell 3 basis points to 3.855%, while the benchmark 10-year yield declined 2.1 basis points to 4.224%.Oil prices also moved lower, with Brent crude falling 1.7% to $104.20 a barrel. Traders weighed the potential impact of US sanctions relief on oil supply against attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Article Summary: Kospi plunges 7.49% as technology stocks come under heavy selling pressure. The country’s exchange operator triggered a five-minute trading halt on programme sell orders after a sharp drop in index futures. The pressure on Asian equities followed a technology-led sell-off on Wall Street after US consumer price inflation accelerated.

Article Title: Heavy rain lashes Delhi-NCR, IMD issues orange alert
Article Text:
Heavy rain and thunderstorms impacted multiple areas of Delhi-NCR on Thursday

(With Agency Inputs)





NEW DELHI: Heavy rain lashed several parts of Delhi-NCR on Thursday, with thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds sweeping across the region.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued an orange alert for the national capital.The weather department forecast rainfall of 5-15 mm per hour, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds blowing at 40-60 kmph.The alert remained in force until 2 pm, with intermittent spells of rain expected in several parts of Delhi, the IMD said.The minimum temperature in the city settled at 23.3 degrees Celsius, 3.7 degrees above normal. The maximum temperature is expected to hover around 29 degrees Celsius, bringing down daytime temperatures, it said.Experts attributed the sudden spell of rain to a western disturbance and a cyclonic circulation over adjoining areas.They said the conditions were part of a normal post-monsoon weather pattern, with Delhi and other parts of the region likely to receive intermittent showers.
Article Summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued an orange alert for the national capital. Rainfall of 5-15 mm per hour, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds. Minimum temperature in the city settled at 23.3 degrees Celsius, 3.7 degrees above normal.

Article Title: CBI arrests SFIO deputy director, advocate in Rs 1 crore bribe case linked to DHFL scam probe
Article Text:
The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. (Representative image)





CHENNAI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has arrested a deputy director-level officer of the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, posted in Chennai, a Delhi-based advocate and the advocate’s relative for allegedly demanding a Rs 1 crore bribe to favour a complainant in an investigation into the DHFL scam.The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch who is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai, advocate Bharat Sharma of New Delhi, and Aryan Sharma, a relative of the advocate, after laying a trap. The arrests followed the advocate’s alleged receipt of Rs 20 lakh from the complainant as part payment of the demanded bribe on behalf of the SFIO officer.According to the CBI, the case was registered against Tanwar, the advocate and others following allegations that they had demanded Rs 1 crore from the complainant to allegedly favour him in an investigation into the DHFL scam being conducted by the SFIO.The CBI verified the complaint before registering the case on Tuesday. It subsequently laid a trap and arrested the three accused after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant on behalf of the SFIO officer.The CBI also conducted searches at the premises of the public servant and the advocate and recovered incriminating material related to the case.The case has been registered under Section 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, relating to criminal conspiracy, and Sections 7 and 7A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Article Summary: The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. Tanwar is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai. The CBI laid a trap after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan, who gave $1.48 million to a Hawaii hospital through Chan Zuckerberg Initiative; on 10 years of association with the island community: What began as a desire to .
Article Text:
Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan funding healthcare infrastructure

More than $4 million donated to Wilcox by Chan Zuckerberg Initiative

Health care the biggest focus

Housing, schools and local jobs

‘Meaningful giving begins with listening’

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan have donated $1.48 million to Hawaii’s Wilcox Medical Center, the latest contribution in what Chan described as a 10-year philanthropic relationship with the island community of Kauaʻi. The donation was made via the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative and will help fund a mobile MRI unit and a new 3D mammography machine at Wilcox Medical Center, according to Hawaii Pacific Health. The gift comes as Chan reflects on a decade of philanthropy in Kauaʻi. In a message published by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, Chan said, “What began as a desire to give back to a place we call home has grown into lasting partnerships with organizations dedicated to strengthening communities, caring for local families, and stewarding the people and places that make Kauaʻi so special.According to the initiative, 2026 marks 10 years of philanthropic work on Kauaʻi, with more than $100 million committed to over 100 local organisations and more than $57 million invested directly on the island.Wilcox Medical Center said the $1.48 million donation will support two key imaging projects. The donation made by Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan will pay for a MRI unit and a new 3D mammography machine. The mobile unit for MRI will work as a stopgap while the hospital renovates its existing MRI suite which is said to complete in coming eight months.For the uninitiated, Wilcox performs more than 4,000 MRI scans a year, and the temporary unit will keep those exams available during the work. The 3D mammography unit, along with the room renovations needed to install it, will support breast cancer screening. Wilcox says it was the first medical center on Kauaʻi to offer 3D mammograms, in 2010, and it performed more than 8,500 mammograms last year. The hospital notes that the clearer 3D images are especially valuable in Hawaiʻi, where many women have dense breast tissue.Wilcox CEO Jen Chahanovich said the couple has repeatedly stepped forward to make sure the community has access to the best medical technology.According to Hawaii Pacific Health, the latest contribution is the couple’s second donation specifically aimed at expanding imaging technology at the hospital. Chan, a paediatrician, and Zuckerberg, the founder and CEO of Meta Platforms, have now made five contributions to Wilcox programmes and services totalling more than $4 million.Previous donations have supported telemedicine initiatives, Covid-19 relief efforts, and renovations of the Wilcox Emergency Department and Trauma Center.Health and wellbeing is the largest area of investment. It includes a $10 million commitment to the University of Hawaiʻi medical school’s Kauaʻi Medical Training Track, which offers full tuition scholarships to future physicians who agree to practice on the island after residency. The program has 22 doctors in training and has graduated its first cohort of five. Support has also gone to a new CT scanner at Wilcox, urgent care expansion on the North Shore, and mental health services for families.Beyond health, the couple’s giving has covered affordable housing, which accounts for nearly a quarter of the total, along with education and youth, food production and distribution, workforce development, cultural lands and emergency relief. Most grants from the Chan Zuckerberg Kauaʻi Community Fund of the Hawaiʻi Community Foundation are unrestricted, so nonprofits can decide how to spend them. Koʻolau Ranch, the couple’s island home, has created 189 local jobs, the initiative said.In her message marking the decade-long milestone, Chan said the family’s approach has been shaped by conversations with residents, community leaders and service providers. “Throughout the past ten years, we’ve learned that meaningful giving begins with listening,” she wrote.The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative said its Kauaʻi philanthropy has supported 101 organisations through 296 grants, focusing on areas including health and wellbeing, affordable housing, education, workforce development, food security and emergency relief.Chan added that the chance to learn from, volunteer with and build relationships across the community had been “one of the greatest gifts of this journey.”
Article Summary: The donation was made via the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative and will help fund a mobile MRI unit and a new 3D mammography machine at Wilcox Medical Center. The gift comes as Chan reflects on a decade of philanthropy in Kauaʻi. Chan, a paediatrician, and Zuckerberg, the founder and CEO of Meta Platforms, have now made five contributions to Wilcox totalling more than $4 million.
